event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit a moment, [player]. I baked a dozen scones for a village that buys six.

event.tilda_heart5.1.text: You're eating it without flinching. Felix flinches. He says it's the butter. It isn't the butter.
event.tilda_heart5.1.why: affectionate jab at her oldest friend; player as the good customer

event.tilda_heart5.2.text: Take the mashed potato home, too. I made that for nobody in particular either.
event.tilda_heart5.2.why: matches the item given; admits she cooks for company that never comes

event.tilda_heart2.0.text: Oh, [player]! Just the account I wanted. Come here, I've something to hand over.

event.tilda_heart2.1.text: My mother's cauliflower gratin. She taught it by hand, never wrote it down. Don't thank me. Bring me a cauliflower someday.
event.tilda_heart2.1.why: the gift; she prefers being owed to being thanked

event.hall_dance.3.text: Nobody asked for credit for any of this. So I'm giving it, in the good chalk, under every name in this room.
event.hall_dance.3.why: the slate as the village's memory of the roof

event.hall_dance.10.text: Into the hall box, every coin. Except one. Marcus, that one's for the ladder.
event.hall_dance.10.why: she gives her winnings away and sets up Marcus's dance

event.story_notes_tilda.intro.text: Oh. Oh, it's you. Stand there a moment and look innocent with me.
event.story_notes_tilda.intro.why: caught in the act, recruits the player as accomplice

dlg.story.notes.tilda.0.text: Tilda slides a folded note under a door and straightens up. Neither of you moves.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.0.why: narration of only what the player sees

dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.text: ...Well. Now you know who's been doing it. Not a word to Wren.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.why: secret kept from the village's other gossip

dlg.story.notes.tilda.c2.text: Slip a note back. Unsigned, obviously.

dlg.story.notes.tilda.r0.text: ...A smile. No chalk, no receipt. That's the hardest kind to put on a slate.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r0.why: a smile as a kindness she cannot record

dlg.story.notes.tilda.r1.text: Don't thank me, I'd rather you owed me. ...Oh, now I'm flustered. I'll go rearrange something.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r1.why: she dislikes thanks; warmth through embarrassment

event.story_notes_tilda.after.text: Signing a kindness is just sending a bill. ...Two more doors before closing. Don't follow me.
event.story_notes_tilda.after.why: why she stays anonymous, in shop terms; a thread

event.story_scarecrows.intro.text: [player]! You're judging. Be completely fair, by which I mean pick mine.

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0.text: Mine is smiling. Crows can't stand a cheerful face. That's simply known.

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.2.text: Well? Whose scarecrow is guarding the fields this fall?

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r0.text: Ha! Taste! Take the runner-up home. It'll stand in your field being thoughtful at the crows.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r0.why: gracious winner, ribbing Dorian's quiet scarecrow

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2.text: A tie. Coward. Take one anyway, and we'll both be wounded together.

event.story_scarecrows.after.text: {if choice:scarecrow.tilda}I won. I'm not smug. I'm radiant. Rematch next fall.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.dorian}He won. I'll say it once, quietly. Rematch next fall.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.tie}A tie. I'm not speaking to you, with love. Rematch next fall.{else}The crows chose both. Wise birds. They're on the slate for diplomacy.{/if}{/if}{/if}
event.story_scarecrows.after.why: each outcome lands; a rematch is promised

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.1.text: Dorian. Is that my prize pumpkin? I've been blaming the goats all week, out loud!

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r0.text: Kindly, then. But he's on the slate for a pie. Mushrooms optional.

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r2.text: You take the heavy end, Dorian takes the guilt. I'll carry the conversation.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.1.text: Marcus! Is that my prize pumpkin? I blamed the goats. I apologized to a goat.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.text: Kindly. Fine. But he owes me a pie, and I've seen him measure. It'll be exact.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.why: debt plus a joke about the carpenter

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r2.text: You and Marcus take the ends. I'll walk ahead and tell everyone it was the goats.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1.text: Felix. Is that my prize pumpkin? You don't even like vegetables!

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r0.text: Kindly. Fine. He owes me a pie, and if there's a fish in it, I'll know.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r2.text: You take the heavy end. Felix can carry the excuses. They weigh more.

event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.text: Lanterns up, everyone. Not lit yet. Wait for the bell. Felix, I mean you.

event.tilda_heart4.intro.text: Come around the counter. Nobody comes back here but me. Mind the cat, it's on duty.

dlg.tilda.slate.0.text: This is the slate. Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. Marcus is two planks ahead of Odalys. She doesn't know yet.

dlg.tilda.slate.1.text: And this blank bit is yours. What shall I write under your name?

dlg.tilda.slate.r0.text: A thank-you. Hard to cash, and I'll never spend it. My favorite currency.

dlg.tilda.slate.r1.text: A joke! On my slate! ...Oh, that's good. Don't tell anyone I laughed in the shop.

dlg.tilda.slate.r2.text: A promise. I'll write it small. I'll hold it large.

event.tilda_heart4.after.text: {if choice:slate.thanks}A thank-you, in chalk. I'll never wipe it, so don't make me.{else}{if choice:slate.joke}A joke on the slate. Nobody's dared. Wren will be furious she didn't think of it.{else}A promise. I hold everyone to everything, kindly. Mostly kindly.{/if}{/if} Now you're on it, you have to come back.
event.tilda_heart4.after.why: closes each branch; debts mean people return

adds.text: Nobody sits in a shop. They lean, they pay, the bell goes twice. You sat.
adds.why: her real want (a customer who sits) said sideways

adds.text: Same chair on Thursday? I'll bake fewer scones. That's a lie, but a polite one.
adds.why: ends on a promise with a day attached

adds.text: She wrote down one recipe in her whole life. I know roughly where it is. I haven't looked.
adds.why: plants the recipe card for heart 8; ends the scene

threads.tilda_heart5: Whether the player comes back Thursday, and who else Tilda keeps baking extra for.
threads.tilda_heart2: Where the one recipe Tilda's mother wrote down is, and why Tilda has never looked.
threads.story_notes_tilda: Which two doors get Tilda's next notes today.
threads.story_scarecrows: Next fall's rematch, and what Tilda will add to her scarecrow.
threads.tilda_heart4: What the rest of the slate says about everyone else.

notes: tilda_heart5: title says scones but the effect gives food.mashed_potato x2; I made line .2 name the mashed potato so text and item agree.
tilda_heart2: my added last line says her mother wrote down only one recipe; heart 8's card is it. The gratin was taught by hand, so no contradiction.
story_pumpkin_*: the closing line by Dorian/Marcus/Felix talks about the speaker in third person ('He's returning it...'); it reads like narration and should be [narration] or rewritten by them.
hall_dance: Wren says 'seven winters' of the roof pool; canon says six winters.
